facts.text: The upstream class is the ImSwitch positioner manager for the UC2 ESP32 stage: it takes the RS232 manager named by managerProperties['rs232device'] and uses its _esp32.motor and _esp32.home
ESP32Manager imports uc2rest as uc2, with the comment pip install UC2-REST
ESP32Manager builds its ESP32 client as uc2.UC2Client with the configured serial port
The stage's per-axis step sizes are calibrated in µm/step, are read from the positioner setup (stepsizeX, stepsizeY, stepsizeZ, stepsizeA) and default to 1
The setup-file reference's example ESP32StageManager properties set stepsizeX 0.396, stepsizeY 0.396 and stepsizeZ 0.3125
The positioner controller documents the requested per-axis target and the position after the move in µm
PositionerController._readPosition takes the per-axis µm position from manager.getPosition() and falls back to the manager's position property when that raises or returns no dict

The move() docstring says that with is_blocking=True it blocks until the motor has reached the new position and that a TimeoutError is raised when the motor has not reached it after timeout; timeout defaults to gTIMEOUT
The module constant gTIMEOUT is 100

The XYZ branch adds the per-axis stage offset to an absolute target and sends one _motor.move_xyz call with the speed, acceleration, enable, blocking and timeout arguments, without using its return value
After _motor.move_xyz returns, the XYZ branch writes the commanded absolute target, or the cached position plus the commanded displacement, into the cached _position
The stage's minimum and maximum positions are positioner setup values: minX/maxX, minY/maxY and minZ/maxZ come from managerProperties and default to -inf and inf
Soft limits are enabled per axis by limitXenabled, limitYenabled and limitZenabled, which also default to false
The single-axis X, Y and Z branches of move() refuse a target below the axis minimum or above its maximum when that axis's limit is enabled
The combined XYZ branch applies no soft-limit check
getPosition() builds a new dict from _motor.get_position() minus the per-axis stage offset; when the query raises, it logs the error and returns the cached _position object itself
The position property of the positioner manager base class returns the cached _position
getDevicePositionAxis documents _motor.get_position() as the live raw device position, read directly from the ESP32 firmware
stopAll() calls _motor.stop() with no axis, the all-axis stop
forceStop() dispatches an axis to stop_x/stop_y/stop_z/stop_a and anything else to stopAll()
PositionerController.stopAllAxes, documented as immediately stopping all axes of the positioner, calls forceStop('all')
cancelZStageSync, documented as stopping an in-progress Z-sync run and halting all motors, sets the sync's cancel event and calls stopAll()
The collision handler's _stopAllMotors, documented as immediately stopping every positioner, calls stopAll() on each positioner that has it
The clone's agent guide lists stopAxis and stopAllAxes as the emergency stop for a move
The clone's agent guide warns that a stage which is moving when its command stream breaks does not stop cleanly
closeEvent() is empty
The constructor enables the motors with isEnable and enableauto from the setup, both defaulting to true
The constructor commands a -1 then +1 relative move on every configured axis and optionally homes on startup
With frameHomeOnStart set in the setup, the constructor starts the frame-homing procedure
frameHomingProcedure runs the homing in a new thread unless is_blocking is true
MIN_SAFE_Z_LIFT_HOMING = 3000 is the minimum distance (µm) Z is lifted out of the bottom before XY are homed, so the stage cannot knock the objective into the sample during the homing sweep
The frame-homing procedure always lifts Z by at least MIN_SAFE_Z_LIFT_HOMING before homing XY so the stage cannot drive the objective into the sample
The repository also defines the StandaMotor class in its interfaces package

safe_state.description: stopAll() -> _motor.stop(), the upstream's immediate stop of all axes, was sent, and two device position queries 0.2 s apart afterwards returned the same X, Y and Z; a failed query (the upstream's cached fallback) or a position that still changes leaves the e-stop SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held. The A axis gets the same stop but is not confirmed, and the clone does not show whether the stop also switches the motor drivers off.
